name: Vanderbilt Mansion

dates.altered: A National Historic Site since December 18, 1940 and operated by the National Park Service with the original furnishings in place; the Vanderbilt Pavilion beside it, also by McKim, Mead & White, housed the family during construction.
dates.note: Wikipedia gives 'Built 1896-99'; a conservation firm's project page read the same day says 'built from 1896 to 1899' and an architects' page says 'constructed in 1897'. The last is a single year inside the range and is not treated as a disagreement.

refs.title: Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site - Wikipedia
refs.note: Gives the architects as 'McKim, Mead & White, Robert H. Robertson', the style as 'Beaux-Arts', the area as 211 acres and the National Historic Site designation of December 18, 1940.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 66000059; added and designated a historic district October 15, 1966; New York State Register reference no. 02707.000015, as the Wikipedia infobox prints it
refs.note: Read from the infobox. The listing is of the district, so the number names the site rather than the house alone.

refs.title: Vanderbilt Mansion - Building Conservation Associates
refs.note: The conservators' own project page: 'The grand Beaux-Arts estate has 54 rooms and is constructed of of Indiana Limestone.' A room count from a consultant, recorded as one.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2 as an addition to beaux-arts-american: the smallest of the great Vanderbilt houses, kept as a museum by the National Park Service since 1940, which is what makes its fabric described rather than remembered. No HABS survey was found for it.
